summary: Cats have a real space story. In 1963 France launched a Paris stray tuxedo cat, Félicette, on a rocket. She is still the only cat known to have flown to space and survived. Cats' mid-air twisting reflex also inspired how NASA-funded researchers studied body rotation for astronauts. A cat's purr is a low rumble of about 25–150 Hz, but the "purring heals bones" claim is not proven. Suggested angle for Space Is Weird: cats in space, with a purr fact as a bonus.

facts.claim: Félicette, a French tuxedo cat, became the first cat in space on 18 October 1963, launched on a Véronique rocket by France's CERMA. She is still the only cat known to have completed and survived a spaceflight.
facts.source_title: Britannica – Who was the first cat in space?

facts.claim: She was a Paris stray chosen from a group of 14 cats, apparently for her calm temperament. She was known as C341 before the flight.

The launch was from the Sahara in Algeria, just after 8am local time (8:09 am per Wikipedia). She experienced about 9.5 g, almost double the g-force Apollo astronauts felt at launch to the Moon. Local time was not verified against IST, so avoid giving an IST launch time.
Electrodes were implanted in her skull and probes monitored her heart during launch, flight and re-entry. She survived re-entry and landed safely by parachute after a trip of under 20 minutes.
A story says another cat, Felix, was meant to fly but escaped on launch day and Félicette replaced him. This is a retelling, not firmly documented, so present it as 'reportedly'.
facts.source_title: Space.com – On this day in space, Oct. 18

facts.claim: Félicette was euthanized about two months after the flight so scientists could examine her brain and body. Mention gently or skip. A bronze statue of her now stands at the International Space University in Strasbourg, France.

The 'falling cat' righting reflex was studied by NASA-funded researchers in the 1960s. In 1968 a gymnast on a trampoline mimicked a falling cat (photographed by Ralph Crane for LIFE), and astronauts are still trained to twist their bodies like cats to turn around in microgravity.

In parabolic-flight microgravity tests, cats with a developed righting reflex kept orienting for the first few seconds. Kittens whose reflex was not yet developed floated upside-down. Without gravity, cats cannot properly 'land on their feet'.
facts.source_title: Nagoya J. Med. Sci. 1995 – Disorientation of animals in microgravity

facts.claim: Cats purr through intermittent signalling of the laryngeal and diaphragmatic muscles, on both inhale and exhale, at roughly 25–150 Hz.
facts.source_title: Scientific American – Why do cats purr?

facts.claim: Purring is not only a sign of happiness. It is more plausibly communication and possible self-soothing/self-healing. The 'purr heals bones' idea is a hypothesis based on low-frequency vibration studies, not proven.
Big cats such as lions, tigers, leopards and jaguars roar rather than purr.

avoid: Do not say Félicette launched on 24 or 21 October 1963. Gizmodo gives Oct 24 and a CBC snippet gives a different date, while Britannica, Space.com, Sky at Night and Wikipedia say 18 October.

Altitude differs by source: about 130 miles (~209 km) per Space.com and Gizmodo, 157 km per CatCognition. Say 'roughly 150–200 km' or 'well above the 100 km space boundary' instead of an exact figure.

Flight duration varies by source: under 20 minutes (Nautilus), about 15 minutes (Gizmodo), 13 minutes (CBC), ~5 minutes of weightlessness (CatCognition). Say 'a quarter-hour or so', or avoid a precise number.
Do not claim 'cats purr to heal their bones' as fact. It is unproven. Also avoid 'purring helps astronauts', since the VetRadar claim is unverified.
Do not say Félicette was the first animal in space. Fruit flies flew in 1947, and many animals including dogs and monkeys came before her.
Do not call her 'Félix' without context. Media nicknamed her Félix after the flight, and the original named candidate was a different cat, Felix.
Do not claim there was a successful cat flight after Félicette. Reports of a follow-up cat flight that killed the cat come from a single blog (CatCognition) and are unverified.
Do not state a precise Indian-time launch time. The local-time-to-IST conversion for Algeria in 1963 was not verified.
Avoid the 'cats have nine lives because of purring' folk claim.
